meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen's essay. Why was a zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
Had to. Who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
I'm not here for compliments. Show me what you have besides a score.
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
I accept nothing today. The company behind your checker says not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have, Hale?
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen's zero. What else do you have?
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
Then end it, or answer me. Owen.
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm not your counsel, Hale. I'm Owen's mother, and the zero comes off today. What else do you have?
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not pausing anything, and I'm not grading you. You've shown me a score, nothing else. Is there a document?
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Show me.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Under 4.1, did anyone put this to Owen before the zero went in?
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
A misquote from memory isn't a fabrication. Search it yourself, you say, so what else is there?

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, and a seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck." I'll read those notes myself.

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.
Timed writing under pressure isn't a weekend with time to revise. Students improve in two months. Put it all on paper and send it to me tonight.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. A private rewrite, to put this behind him, and nothing on his record. I want 4.4 and the zero coming off in writing tonight, and the rest goes in my email.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. In writing tonight, and I'll be reading it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed tonight that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite before December 1 under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want that confirmed in writing, the zero removed, and the documents you showed me sent to me on paper. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1, with nothing on his record and the terms in writing tonight, while still wanting the zero removed and your documents on paper; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and it was reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the document version history with its exact times, because it was dated and she could check it on the screen herself.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score as your reason for the zero, because she could not verify it and it let her go straight to your procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night entries on October 28 before the deadline, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Say in your first sentence that you entered the zero before calling her, and put the version history on the table before the score is ever mentioned.
